original_question: (S. Tabachnikov) Let γ ⊂ RP2 be a smooth closed strictly convex curve, and let F be a smooth foliation by convex closed curves in its exterior neighbourhood, including γ as a leaf. The intersection of every tangent line to γ with the leaves of F define a local involution on this line, the point of tangency being a fixed point. Suppose that these involutions are projective transformations for all tangent lines of γ. Then γ is an ellipse, and the foliation consists of ellipses that form a pencil.
target_in_paper: Conjecture 4.3 in §4.2.1, “Around the Birkhoff conjecture,” of the current arXiv HTML version; the same statement appears as Conjecture 3.3 in §3.2.1 of the 72-page arXiv v1 PDF, p. 19. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1804.03737))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures essentially all of the official statement: the ambient space RP^2, the smooth closed strictly convex curve γ, the smooth foliation F by convex closed curves in an exterior neighbourhood with γ as a leaf, the induced involutions on tangent lines, the hypothesis that these involutions are projective on every tangent line, and the conclusion that γ should be an ellipse and the foliation should come from a pencil of ellipses. It is very close to verbatim. ([upcommons.upc.edu](https://upcommons.upc.edu/bitstreams/d858abf8-e232-45e3-a199-3adac6cf7893/download))
missing_details: The paper states this as a conjecture/open problem, so the stand-alone version should be phrased explicitly as a question (“Is it true that ... ?”) rather than as an asserted implication. ([upcommons.upc.edu](https://upcommons.upc.edu/bitstreams/d858abf8-e232-45e3-a199-3adac6cf7893/download))

Because F is only given in an exterior neighbourhood of γ, the induced map on each tangent line is only a local involution (a germ near the tangency point), not a globally defined involution on the whole line. ([upcommons.upc.edu](https://upcommons.upc.edu/bitstreams/d858abf8-e232-45e3-a199-3adac6cf7893/download))

To make the construction self-contained, one should spell out the involution: on a tangent line L at p ∈ γ, a nearby point x on L is mapped to the other intersection point of L with the leaf of F through x; p is the fixed point. This is implicit in the paper’s wording. ([upcommons.upc.edu](https://upcommons.upc.edu/bitstreams/d858abf8-e232-45e3-a199-3adac6cf7893/download))

It is helpful to make explicit that ‘projective transformation’ means a projective automorphism of the tangent line viewed as a projective line, and that ‘pencil’ means a pencil of conics in RP^2. The paper uses this terminology without expanding it there. ([upcommons.upc.edu](https://upcommons.upc.edu/bitstreams/d858abf8-e232-45e3-a199-3adac6cf7893/download))
refined_question: Is the following conjecture true? Let γ ⊂ RP^2 be a smooth closed strictly convex curve, and let F be a smooth foliation by convex closed curves in an exterior neighbourhood of γ, with γ itself as one leaf. For each point p ∈ γ and its tangent line L = T_pγ, define a local involution ι_L of L near p by sending a point x ∈ L near p to the other intersection point of L with the leaf of F passing through x; the point p is fixed by ι_L. Assume that for every tangent line L to γ, the germ ι_L is a projective transformation of the projective line L. Must γ be an ellipse, and must all leaves of F be ellipses belonging to a single pencil of conics? ([upcommons.upc.edu](https://upcommons.upc.edu/bitstreams/d858abf8-e232-45e3-a199-3adac6cf7893/download))
justification: The draft is clearly targeting the paper’s official Conjecture 4.3/3.3, because its wording matches that conjecture almost exactly and sits in the subsection on Birkhoff-type billiard problems. It is not the broader surrounding Birkhoff material in Problem 4.2/3.2, and it should not be replaced by the narrower Problem 4.5/3.5, which asks only for the special case where the foliation has a rational or algebraic first integral. The paragraph immediately following the conjecture gives the nearby context the paper itself attaches to it: the converse is a classical Desargues theorem; the isometric special case yields the outer-billiard Birkhoff conjecture; and the generalized form is linked by projective duality to projective/inner billiards. The paper does not supply an explicit equivalent reformulation, only a converse observation and a special case, so no alternate equivalent formulation should be invented here. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1804.03737))
